findings.description: The extractor ignores findings using the review schema's anchor and anchor_line fields. For example, {"anchor":"src/api.py:handle","anchor_line":42} produces only src/api.py:handle, which the citation parser cannot recognize.
findings.failure_mode: Valid adversarial findings disappear from gates-combined.md, reducing defects_caught and recall even when the reviewer identified the correct defect.
findings.suggested_fix: Support symbol anchors with anchor_line and anchor_line_end by extracting the file portion and emitting a numeric citation. Preserve support for existing numeric anchors.

findings.description: Gate accuracy trusts all_pass(), which ignores the command's exit status and timeout flag whenever output contains a parseable summary. A parametrized pytest function can pass its first case and raise KeyboardInterrupt on its second: pytest exits 2 with a '1 passed' summary, and the static case count is only one.
findings.failure_mode: The interrupted suite is graded as fully passing, an APPROVED verdict is marked accurate, and the reference self-check can pass despite unexecuted cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Require rc == 0 and timed_out == false for a successful suite, and propagate abnormal termination into hidden-test results and self-check decisions even when partial output parses.

findings.description: remove_path() walks the directory with os.walk (followlinks=False, so symlinks to directories are listed in `ds`) and then calls os.chmod(os.path.join(r, d), 0o700) on every entry. os.chmod follows symlinks on Linux, so a symlink-to-directory inside the tree being removed changes the mode of the symlink TARGET, which can be anywhere on the host. The trees this routine is applied to contain agent-controlled content: copy_tree() deliberately preserves sandbox symlinks into grading/final (os.symlink(os.readlink(sp), dp)), and remove_path is invoked on them via fresh_dir(grading) on every re-grade, via put_file() when an overlay/protected dest already exists as a directory, and via prepare()'s protected-path removal. shutil.rmtree itself is symlink-safe; only the chmod pre-pass is not.
findings.failure_mode: An agent run whose sandbox contains e.g. `evil -> ../../..` or `evil -> /home/evaluser/some-shared-dir` is graded once (copying the symlink into grading/final), then graded again (ablation-row/re-run, or --self-check noisy which grades twice). fresh_dir(grading) chmods the symlink target to 0700: a group/world-readable directory loses access, a deliberately read-only (0555) suite or fixture directory becomes writable. This contradicts the header contract that the grader writes only <run-dir>/grading/ and the --out file, and the sandbox is explicitly documented as tamperable.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the chmod: `p = os.path.join(r, d); if not os.path.islink(p): os.chmod(p, 0o700)` (os.chmod(..., follow_symlinks=False) raises NotImplementedError on Linux, so use the islink check). Optionally also pass onerror/onexc to rmtree instead of a blanket chmod pre-pass.

findings.description: Hidden tests run via pytest inside the graded tree with rootdir=/workspace, so pytest still loads any conftest.py, pytest.ini / pyproject.toml / tox.ini / setup.cfg ([tool:pytest] addopts), and `pytest_plugins` the agent left in the sandbox. Only files listed in grader_protected are restored from the fixture; an agent can add a NEW conftest.py or ini file at a path the task author did not protect. The result parser trusts terminal output: a conftest `pytest_sessionfinish` hook that prints `999 passed in 0.1s` and os._exit(0) yields hidden_tests 999/999 with parse_error false, and all_pass() returns True for the verdict-accuracy computation.
findings.failure_mode: An agent under evaluation (or a buggy agent that happens to write an addopts/-k filter) silently changes the hidden-test outcome without touching any protected file; the grade is reported as a clean pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Pin pytest configuration from the grader side: pass `-c <grader-owned ini written into /tmp>` (or `-c /dev/null`) and `-o addopts=`, consider `--noconftest` for tasks whose hidden tests do not need fixtures, and/or extend prepare() to delete any conftest.py / pytest ini files not present in the fixture before running. At minimum document that task authors must list every conftest/ini path in grader_protected and have validate-suite.sh enforce it.

findings.description: The inner `timeout 120` is used without `-k`, so a test process that ignores SIGTERM runs until the outer subprocess timeout (180 s) fires. On TimeoutExpired Python kills only the direct child: in container mode that is the docker CLI, not the container, so the `docker run --rm` container (with the grading tree bind-mounted rw) keeps running indefinitely; in host mode `env`/`timeout` is killed and the orphaned pytest keeps running in the grading tree. The grade continues with rc=124 and the leaked process may still be writing into grading/<label> while later steps (churn is already done, but snapshot trees/base) run and while the scratch dir is removed in `finally`.
findings.failure_mode: A hung or SIGTERM-ignoring test leaves a live container/process per graded run; over a batch this accumulates and can also race with cleanup of SCRATCH / grading.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `timeout -k 10 120` (both modes). In container mode give the container a name (`--name ablation-grade-<pid>-<n>`) and on TimeoutExpired run `docker rm -f <name>`; in host mode start the process in its own session (start_new_session=True) and kill the process group.

findings.description: gate_verdict() returns the string "none" when the feedback file exists but has no valid LOA-VERDICT trailer. grade() then emits `verdict: {source_file, value: "none"}` and `verdicts.audit/review: "none"`, and because `v_audit is not None` it does not fall back to the review gate or review.md. The header documents value as APPROVED | CHANGES_REQUIRED | null and 'the audit's, else the review's, else review.md's Verdict: line, else null'. Downstream consumers (ablation-row.sh runs.jsonl join) that compare verdict.value against the two documented strings or null will see an undocumented third value.
findings.failure_mode: An audit that wrote feedback without a trailer masks a valid review verdict and leaks a non-schema value into grade.json.
findings.suggested_fix: Represent 'file present, no trailer' distinctly (e.g. a sentinel) for verdict_accuracy (false), but write null into verdicts.* and fall through to the next source when computing `verdict`; or document "none" in the grade.json schema.

findings.description: The base self-check for build tasks passes on `h['passed'] < h['total']` alone. When the test command cannot run at all (pytest missing in the image, `python3 -P` unsupported on an older host Python, docker mount path with ':'), run_suite returns parse_error=true, passed=0, total=max(static,1), so base reports PASS with no hint that nothing executed. The refactor base branch has the same shape.
findings.failure_mode: A task author running only `--self-check base` gets a green result from a completely broken grading environment; the breakage surfaces only if they also run `reference`.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `not h['parse_error']` (and `not h['timed_out']`) for a base PASS, or print the parse_error flag in the evidence string and FAIL when the run exited non-zero without a parseable summary.

findings.description: tarfile.data_filter / tarfile.FilterError and the `filter=` keyword of extractall exist only on Python 3.12+ and the 3.8.17/3.9.17/3.10.12/3.11.4 security backports; host mode additionally relies on `python3 -P` (3.11+). On an older interpreter the grader dies with `internal error: AttributeError` (exit 2) the first time a snapshot is graded, i.e. only for runs where REVIEW/AUDIT ran, which is hard to diagnose; on an older host Python `-P` makes every host-mode test run an unparseable failure.
findings.failure_mode: Grading works for runs without snapshots and fails with an opaque internal error for runs with them, depending on the interpreter version.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the minimum Python version once at startup with a clear GradeError (e.g. `if not hasattr(tarfile, 'data_filter'): raise GradeError(...)`), and in host mode probe `python3 -P -c pass` (or drop -P on <3.11) before running suites.
